says: In next/, a lifeCell step holds the life lock while its fact write waits for the outbox lock, and the outbox flush holds that lock across a control HTTP call with no timeout, so a flush that dialed a hung workerd just before a replace delays the SIGTERM and every fold, the stop included, until the HTTP call ends.
proof: local-dev.ts:73 runs then (record, then outbox.add under the outbox's turn.withPermit at :319) inside the life lock; local-dev.ts:350 calls send(row) inside the outbox's turn.withPermit; dev.ts:221 executes the control request with no timeout.
cost: Rarely, quitting the app or ending an over-limit runtime waits up to Node fetch's default timeout, about 5 minutes.
